svg.title: Portfolio Platform: system architecture
svg.desc: System design overview of yuqi.site. A system map shows how Ask AI, content publishing, notifications, visitor analytics and the MCP tools connect, and the lanes below repeat those links in place: the pgvector RAG store sits on the boundary between Ask AI, which reads it, and publishing, which writes it; publishing writes the article and its outbox in one PostgreSQL transaction and an outbox relay hands content.notification.* to the notifications Kafka; analytics alerts call the notification service directly. Each lane shows its Next.js UI and the Vercel API route it calls, its Google Cloud Run services next to the PostgreSQL, Redis and OpenSearch stores they own, its Kafka topics and third-party APIs, followed by the Kubernetes exit-path decision record and platform concerns.
svg.text: The map shows how the five systems connect; each lane below shows how one of them works, from the Next.js UI to Cloud Run and the data it owns.

g.text: KNATIVE · MIN 0–1 · MAX 1–2 INSTANCES · CPU PER REQUEST
Cloud Run today, Kubernetes as the exit path
Spiky, low traffic and one maintainer: scale-to-zero and per-request billing beat an always-on cluster.
OCI image per service, run as a Knative Service
A drain call wakes the Kafka consumers
KEDA Kafka scaler on consumer lag
Steady traffic or always-on consumers make a small cluster cheaper.
JWT sessions · owner RBAC · confirm before writes
CSP headers · reCAPTCHA · rate limits · signed URLs
Prometheus + Loki → Grafana · run traces in OpenSearch
GitHub Actions (OIDC) → Cloud Build → Cloud Run
Idempotency keys · outbox · DLQ replay · rebuilds
Scale-to-zero · instance caps · daily AI budget
